title: Silence as Leverage
description: Say less, wait longer, and let the other side fill the gap.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: Silence is uncomfortable, and people rush to fill it — often with information, concessions or a revised offer. A negotiator who can sit in the pause gains without saying a word.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: The urge to end an awkward silence is strong. Whoever speaks first after a proposal often gives something away, so patience becomes a form of power.

sections.title: Real-Life Examples
content: After making an offer, saying nothing until the other side responds.
A pause after hearing a price, which makes the seller justify it.

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: Long pauses that the other side breaks.
A negotiator comfortable not filling every gap.

sections.title: How to Use It
sections.content: Make your point, then stop. Count a few seconds before speaking. Let the other person break the silence.

sections.title: Red Flags
content: Silence used to pressure or intimidate rather than to think.
A pause that is really a tactic to rush you.

sections.title: Defense Strategies
content: You are allowed to sit in silence too.
Do not fill a pause with a concession.

sections.title: Key Lessons
content: Comfort with pauses is an advantage.
